commit_message:
[HAL] Reject buffer view size overflows (#24992)

Rejects dense buffer views when shape multiplication or packed byte-size
calculation exceeds `iree_device_size_t`. Previously, overflowing
dimensions could wrap to a small value and produce an undersized
allocation request.

The size calculation now uses checked multiplication and addition while
preserving zero-dimension behavior and sub-byte element packing. Dense
view creation also verifies that the logical byte length fits within the
backing buffer, and reshape validates element counts before updating
metadata.

Tests cover:

- Shape products that wrap to zero or one.
- Packed-byte multiplication and addition overflow.
- Maximum-size byte and sub-byte element counts.
- Zero dimensions following otherwise overflowing dimensions.
- Dense views larger than their backing buffers.
- Overflowing reshape attempts.
- Native and forced 32-bit `iree_device_size_t` configurations.

Tested with:

- `iree/hal/buffer_view_util_test`
- `iree/hal/string_util_test`
- `iree/tooling/buffer_view_matchers_test`
- `iree/tooling/function_io_test`
- `iree/tooling/numpy_io_test`
- Repository pre-commit hooks for all changed files

The original `iree-run-module` reproducer was not rerun because the
validation build was configured as runtime-only without compiler tools.

This addresses the concrete buffer-view overflow case tracked in #3844.
The broader size-arithmetic audit remains open.

AI agents assisted with understanding the codebase, writing tests, and
reviewing the solution.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Propagate affine QDQ through tensor operations (#24906)

The integer contraction rewrite from #24902 needs dequantize_affine to
be the direct producer of a contraction operand. This PR adds
PropagateAffineQuantization, which moves the tensor ops in between onto
the quantized side, where they also operate on narrower data. It runs
right before each integer QDQ rewrite.

It perform the following transformations:

```
quantize(collapse_shape(x))   ->  collapse_shape(quantize(x))
expand_shape(dequantize(q))   ->  dequantize(expand_shape(q))
pad(dequantize(q), 0.0)       ->  dequantize(pad(q, zp))

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Require output channel reuse for im2col

The im2col control function rejected only convolutions without an
output channel loop, so a depthwise convolution with a unit channel
multiplier, whose output channel loop has extent one, was still
rewritten even though nothing reuses its gathered input. Require an
output channel loop whose extent is not statically one; a dynamic
extent may exceed one and counts as reuse.

Pass the already inferred convolution dimensions to the control
function, so selection uses the same dimensions as the rewrite instead
of inferring them again.

[GlobalOptimization] Require output channel reuse for im2col

The im2col control function rejected only convolutions without an
output channel loop, so a depthwise convolution with a unit channel
multiplier, whose output channel loop has extent one, was still
rewritten even though nothing reuses its gathered input. Require an
output channel loop whose extent is not statically one; a dynamic
extent may exceed one and counts as reuse.

Pass the already inferred convolution dimensions to the control
function, so selection uses the same dimensions as the rewrite instead
of inferring them again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Propagate affine QDQ through tensor operations (#24906)

The integer contraction rewrite from #24902 needs dequantize_affine to
be the direct producer of a contraction operand. This PR adds
PropagateAffineQuantization, which moves the tensor ops in between onto
the quantized side, where they also operate on narrower data. It runs
right before each integer QDQ rewrite.

It perform the following transformations:

```
quantize(collapse_shape(x))   ->  collapse_shape(quantize(x))
expand_shape(dequantize(q))   ->  dequantize(expand_shape(q))
pad(dequantize(q), 0.0)       ->  dequantize(pad(q, zp))
transpose(dequantize(q))      ->  dequantize(q) with its output map permuted
```

Part of #24862

Assisted By: Claude Code

commit_message:
[HAL] Reject buffer view size overflows (#24992)

Rejects dense buffer views when shape multiplication or packed byte-size
calculation exceeds `iree_device_size_t`. Previously, overflowing
dimensions could wrap to a small value and produce an undersized
allocation request.

The size calculation now uses checked multiplication and addition while
preserving zero-dimension behavior and sub-byte element packing. Dense
view creation also verifies that the logical byte length fits within the
backing buffer, and reshape validates element counts before updating
metadata.

Tests cover:

- Shape products that wrap to zero or one.
- Packed-byte multiplication and addition overflow.
- Maximum-size byte and sub-byte element counts.
- Zero dimensions following otherwise overflowing dimensions.
- Dense views larger than their backing buffers.
- Overflowing reshape attempts.
- Native and forced 32-bit `iree_device_size_t` configurations.

Tested with:

- `iree/hal/buffer_view_util_test`
- `iree/hal/string_util_test`
- `iree/tooling/buffer_view_matchers_test`
- `iree/tooling/function_io_test`
- `iree/tooling/numpy_io_test`
- Repository pre-commit hooks for all changed files

The original `iree-run-module` reproducer was not rerun because the
validation build was configured as runtime-only without compiler tools.

This addresses the concrete buffer-view overflow case tracked in #3844.
The broader size-arithmetic audit remains open.

AI agents assisted with understanding the codebase, writing tests, and
reviewing the solution.

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-token quantization to LinalgExt

Convert quantized_decomposed.quantize_per_token and dequantize_per_token
to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and dequantize_affine. Per-token
parameters vary along every input dimension but the last, so they are
indexed by those dimensions and the data path needs no reshape. PT2E
keeps a unit dimension in place of the last input dimension, which is
dropped from the parameters.

Per-token shares its operand checks with per-channel-group. They require
the scale and zero point to have exactly the expected shape, because
PT2E broadcasts unit extents, and decline non-integer storage dtypes
such as !torch.qint8 and quantize scales narrower than 32 bits or than
the input.

Dequantization matches the PT2E reference. The per-token reference adds
the zero point before rounding, so quantize ties with odd zero points
differ from it and from the Torch-to-Linalg lowering, which follows it.

Depends on the torch-mlir ops from llvm/torch-mlir#4765.

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-token dequantization to LinalgExt

Convert quantized_decomposed.dequantize_per_token to
iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine. Per-token parameters vary along every
input dimension but the last, so they are indexed by those dimensions
and the data path needs no reshape. PT2E keeps a unit dimension in place
of the last input dimension, which is dropped from the parameters.

Quantization stays on the Torch-to-Linalg path, because the per-token
reference adds the zero point before rounding, which Torch-to-Linalg
follows and LinalgExt does not. Operands that LinalgExt cannot express
stay there as well.

Per-token shares its operand checks with per-channel-group. They
require the scale and zero point to have exactly the expected shape,
because PT2E broadcasts unit extents, and decline non-integer storage
dtypes such as !torch.qint8.

Depends on the torch-mlir ops from llvm/torch-mlir#4765.

commit_message:
[HAL] Reject buffer view size overflows (#24992)

Rejects dense buffer views when shape multiplication or packed byte-size
calculation exceeds `iree_device_size_t`. Previously, overflowing
dimensions could wrap to a small value and produce an undersized
allocation request.
